\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24 Termination of agreement approved.\par
\par
Responding to a query by Commissioner Latvala, Human Services Director Karen Yatchum indicated that the Pinellas County Sheriff\rquote s Office and other law enforcement agencies have expressed concerns regarding the transition of responsibility for work related to the Sexual Assault Victim Examination (SAVE) Program from the Suncoast Center, Inc. to local hospitals due to anticipated complications in the investigative process.\par
\par
Commissioner Latvala also expressed concerns regarding Suncoast Center\rquote s mental health services and inquired whether residents would be better served by another provider assuming responsibility for the Program; whereupon, Ms. Yatchum discussed the importance of a trauma-informed approach and the organization\rquote s efforts to ensure compliance while under corrective action.\par
\par
In response to queries by Chair Eggers, Ms. Yatchum, with input by Mr. Burton, provided information regarding the County\rquote s contribution to the Program, noting that it is funded through the end of December; and that removal of County funding will not impede the Program. Ms. Yatchum also related that a $40,000.00 annual contribution from each hospital would be needed in order for Suncoast Center, Inc. to continue work related to the SAVE Program instead of transferring responsibility to the hospital system; whereupon, she briefly discussed the procurement process that would be required to seek another Program provider.\par
\par
Ms. Yatchum indicated that she sent a letter to the leadership of each local hospital in July; and that representatives from the majority of the hospitals were present at a community meeting which took place yesterday at Suncoast Center; whereupon, she emphasized that additional meetings will be required before the end of the year to ensure either a successful transition to the hospital system or to coordinate contributions to allow the Program to remain centralized through Suncoast Center, Inc.\par
\par
Discussion ensued, with input by Ms. Yatchum and Mr. Burton, regarding various topics, including the importance of maintaining services for sexual assault victims, yesterday\rquote s community meeting, termination of the agreement, ongoing and future communications with hospital leadership and Suncoast Center, Inc., and responsibility for funding and services. \par
\par
Responding to further queries by Chair Eggers, Ms. Yatchum, with input by Mr. Burton, indicated that today\rquote s vote is required to provide a proper 30-day notice to Suncoast Center, Inc. regarding termination of the agreement.\par
\par
At the Chair\rquote s request, Suncoast Center, Inc. President/CEO Jean Pierre appeared and provided historical information regarding the SAVE Program, budget concerns, operational costs, and shortfalls; whereupon, in response to comments and queries by the members, Ms. Yatchum, with input by Mr. Pierre, discussed the 30-day notice requirement, future coordination meetings, alternative funding options, and previous correspondence regarding the potential transition.\par
\par
In response to queries by Chair Eggers, Ms. Yatchum indicated that work regarding transition planning will continue regardless of whether the Board takes action today; and that she can provide an update at the next Board of County Commissioners meeting; whereupon, Chair Eggers clarified the motion on the table and confirmed that the maker and seconder of the motion still wish to proceed with taking action.\par
\par
Following the vote, Commissioner Scherer suggested that the Chair send an additional letter to hospital leadership emphasizing the importance of this matter; whereupon, Chair Eggers confirmed that there is consensus from the members for him to do so.\cf1\f1\fs22\par
}
title: Termination of the Agreement with Suncoast Center, Inc. for the Sexual Assault Victim Examination Program.

Forward Pinellas, in its role as the Pinellas Planning Council, and the Planners Advisory Committee recommended approval of the amendment. No correspondence has been received. No citizens appeared to be heard. \par
\par
At the request of Chair Eggers, Forward Pinellas Program Planner Emma Wennick referred to a PowerPoint presentation containing maps and photographs, pointed out the location of the subject property, and provided information regarding the proposed amendment, including the property\rquote s existing and proposed land use designations and compatibility with surrounding uses. \par
\par
Responding to comments and queries from members, Planning Section Manager Scott Swearengen discussed the proposed redevelopment of the existing community assembly facility, including improvements to the building, parking, and stormwater infrastructure. He explained that the project would eliminate an existing access point on Keystone Road; that a conditional zoning overlay would limit development intensity and restrict the property's use to a community assembly facility; and that the redevelopment would bring the property into compliance with current County development regulations.\par
\par
In response to comments by Commissioner Nowicki regarding the property's use as a mosque, Mr. Swearengen explained that the County's zoning ordinances classify religious institutions under the broader designation of community assembly facilities; whereupon, Commissioner Nowicki expressed concern regarding overdevelopment in north county and inconsistent designation standards, indicating that previous recommendations for nearby land use designations were denied. \par
\par
Responding to additional queries by the members, Mr. Swearengen indicated that approval of the proposed Countywide Plan Map amendment would allow the property owner to proceed with the site plan review process; whereupon, in response to a query by Commissioner Scherer, he confirmed that no public opposition has been received regarding the request.\f1\fs22\par
}

\ul Approval previously provided by the Chair for a conflict waiver for Shumaker, Loop & Kendrick, LLP\par

Referring to an existing agreement with Shumaker, Loop & Kendrick, LLP, Attorney White indicated that the contract contains a provision which allows the Chair to address waivers of conflict; and that she recently met with the Chair and received approval to process a conflict waiver for the firm to represent a current client regarding a Code Enforcement matter; whereupon, she noted that the attorney representing the client would not be the same attorney utilized by the County; that the waiver relates only to proceedings before the special magistrate; and that the attorney would remove themselves from the case should any litigation ensue.\par
\par
\ul Update regarding time limitation for State of Local Emergency due to mosquito-borne illness\par
\ulnone\par
Referencing the current State of Local Emergency due to mosquito-borne illness, Attorney White clarified that while she previously informed the Board that she believed there was a 42-day limitation, she does not believe that that is the case; whereupon, she indicated that an executive order was issued by the Governor, which concerns both weather-related events and the mosquito-borne illness outbreak.\par

In response to a query by Chair Eggers, Attorney White also explained that authority related to renewing the State of Local Emergency has been delegated to the County Administrator; whereupon, Mr. Burton indicated that he has issued a renewal of the State of Local Emergency; and that, due to the inclusion of Pinellas County in the executive order, an additional renewal may not be necessary.\par
\par
\ul Upcoming closed attorney-client session on October 22\par
\ulnone\par
Attorney White indicated that she is requesting guidance from the Board regarding settlement negotiations or strategies related to litigation expenditures associated with the case of \i African People's Education and Defense Fund, Inc. v. Pinellas County\i0 ; and that a closed attorney-client session has been scheduled for October 22 at 1:00 P.M.; whereupon, in response to a query by Chair Eggers, she confirmed that no action is required today.\cf2\f1\fs22\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\f0\fs24 Mr. Burton explained that recent public records requests submitted to the County have revealed that there is confusion surrounding the separate approvals associated with Case No. CW 26-12, which was approved at the October 13 Board of County Commission (BCC) meeting. He indicated that the Board approved land use and zoning amendments for the applicable subject property in June; and that the item approved at the October 13 BCC meeting only involved a Countywide Plan Map amendment, which was the final step in the process. \par
\par
Referring to a PowerPoint presentation, Zoning and Project Management Division Manager Michael Schoderbock provided an overview of the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA), explaining that the federal law prevents state and local governments from:\par
\par
\pard\fi-360\li360\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Enforcing land use laws that restrict religious exercise\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Treating a religious assembly or institution less favorably than a comparable non-religious assembly\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Discriminating against any specific religion or denomination\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Banning religious assemblies or unreasonably limiting them within a specific area\par
\pard\par
Mr. Schoderbock indicated that, based on the RLUIPA and guidance received from the County Attorney\rquote s Office, staff amended the Land Development Code in 2019 to establish that the classification of \ldblquote meeting hall/community assembly facility\rdblquote includes both religious and non-religious uses and facilities. He then reviewed the public hearing timeline and notification procedures associated with the subject property in question, including mailed notices, newspaper advertisements, and property signage.\par
\par
In response to comments and queries by Chair Eggers and Commissioner Latvala, Mr. Schoderbock provided information regarding the composition of the Local Planning Agency (LPA), the public notification requirements applicable to the case, and the methods used to notify surrounding property owners and the general public.\par
\par
Responding to a query by Commissioner Nowicki, Mr. Schoderbock explained that a public notice sign was posted along East Lake Drive since the subject property\rquote s two-way entrance and exit are located there. He also provided details regarding County requirements for access from roads with lower classifications and clarified that the existing access onto Keystone Road would be removed as part of the proposed redevelopment; whereupon, in response to comments by Commissioner Nowicki, he confirmed that there is no Code or statute definition which defines \ldblquote main access.\rdblquote\par
\par
Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Schoderbock clarified that although the Staff Report refers to the proposed use of the subject property as a community assembly facility, the application and concept plan specifically identified it as a place of worship; whereupon, he provided background information related to the property\rquote s existing use as a place of worship since the early 1990s and briefly discussed the proposed redevelopment, including details regarding improvements to stormwater management, traffic safety, and landscaping.\par
In response to additional comments and queries by the members, Mr. Schoderbock provided information regarding potential measures to increase public awareness of future land use and zoning cases, including expanding the notification radius and making information more accessible online; whereupon, Mr. Burton explained that he requested that the County Attorney's Office review the way in which this case was handled to determine whether there were any legal deficiencies; and that the review found no legal deficiencies and confirmed that all County Code and statutory requirements were met.\par
\par
In response to a query by Commissioner Nowicki regarding the options available to individuals who oppose the approved changes, Attorney White indicated that the Board\rquote s decision remains within the appellate period; that Chapter 163 of Florida Statutes provides affected persons with an opportunity to appeal the Board\rquote s decision in Circuit Court; and that owners of property abutting the subject property would qualify as affected persons. She further clarified that other individuals could file an appeal, although their standing to do so could be contested; whereupon, in response to a query by Chair Eggers regarding options available to the members, Attorney White stated that the Board\rquote s action is final.\par
\par
Thereupon, the following citizens appeared in response to Chair Eggers\rquote call for public comment:\par

\par
At the request of Chair Eggers, St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport Director Mark Sprague provided an overview of the revised project scope, explaining that the project was rescoped to prioritize aging infrastructure; and that the revised project includes a 40,000-square-foot terminal extension and improvements to utilities, roofing, security and boarding areas, lighting, and furnishings.\par
\par
In response to comments and queries by Chair Eggers, Mr. Sprague, with input by Mr. Burton, provided clarifying information regarding the revised project budget and associated design and construction management fees, indicating that the original Request for Proposals was based on a $110 million project budget; that the project estimate had increased to more than $220 million following the completion of 30% schematic drawings; and that the project budget was subsequently rescoped to approximately $145 million.\par
\par
Responding to queries by Commissioners Scott and Scherer, Mr. Sprague indicated that the approximately $14 million previously authorized for design and construction services has not been fully spent; and that C&S Engineers provides design services, while the Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) works with the designer to establish a guaranteed maximum price prior to the beginning of construction.\par
\par
In response to comments by Commissioner Scherer, Assistant County Administrator Blaine Williams provided information regarding the respective roles and responsibilities of the companies involved in the project and measures taken to avoid duplication of services. He also confirmed that, prior to construction, a guaranteed maximum price will be brought back to the Board for approval.\f1\fs22\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24 Settlement approved in accordance with the confidential memorandum dated October 27, 2026.\par

Attorney White introduced the item, indicating that it involves a staff recommendation prepared in response to a settlement demand made to the County by SPCA Tampa Bay; and that the recommendation was outlined in a confidential memorandum previously provided to the Board.\par
\par
In response to a query by Chair Eggers, Attorney White indicated that this item is proceeding under a confidential memorandum since it is a pre-suit settlement discussion, which is confidential in nature; that the item involves attorney-client work product; and that while the Board holds the privilege to waive confidentiality, she recommends against doing so; whereupon, she noted that staff\rquote s recommendation regarding the handling of the demand is contained in the memorandum.\par
\par
Upon Chair Eggers\rquote call for public comment, Connie Laurie, Lithia, waived in opposition against SPCA, and David Glenn, Jr., Seminole, appeared and expressed his concerns.\par
\par
At the request of Chair Eggers, Attorney White provided information regarding the confidentiality of pre-litigation settlement demands under Florida law, including the protection of claims handled through the County\rquote s risk management program and related attorney work product; whereupon, responding to a query by Chair Eggers, she explained that files associated with concluded litigation generally become public, although she would need to verify the applicable timeframe for disclosure of materials associated with a risk management claim.\par
\par
In response to further comments by Chair Eggers, Attorney White indicated that the County received a letter from an attorney representing SPCA Tampa Bay outlining alleged damages exceeding the $250,000.00 ultimately demanded; that staff lacked the authority to accept or reject the demand due to the amount involved; and that SPCA Tampa Bay\rquote s letter and staff\rquote s response have been provided as part of public records.\par
\par
Referencing comments made by Mr. Glenn regarding campaign contributions, Commissioner Peters requested that Attorney White clarify the ethical considerations related to such contributions; whereupon, Attorney White explained that candidates may receive contributions from anyone; that financial campaign contributions are excluded from the definition of gifts under the Florida Ethics Code; and that any contribution which complies with Florida Election Code standards is legitimate if it is not made for a corrupt purpose.\cf1\f1\fs22\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\ul\f0\fs24 Proposed Handbook Amendment - Commissioner Agenda Items (Commissioner Nowicki)\ulnone\par
\par
Chair Eggers indicated that Commissioner Nowicki had brought forth two items for discussion, the first of which involved a proposed amendment to the County Commission handbook; whereupon, Commissioner Flowers expressed support for the existing process for bringing items before the Board and indicated that she did not support adding language to the handbook.\par
\par
Responding to comments and queries by the Chair, Mr. Burton explained that the proposed amendment would allow an individual Commissioner to place an item directly on an upcoming agenda without prior discussion at a work session or direction from the Board; and that he would request that Commissioners follow staff's established timeline for agenda submissions. He also provided information regarding the existing process for requesting that items be placed on future agendas.\par
\par
Commissioner Latvala expressed concerns regarding the proposed amendment and indicated that he supported the existing process with some modifications; whereupon, Commissioner Nowicki indicated that he would not make a motion to amend the handbook if the proposed change did not have the Board's support. He then expressed concerns regarding the handling of his requests to bring items before the Board, citing a previously requested workshop regarding an airport master plan and an email to Mr. Burton concerning an agenda item associated with Keystone Road.\par
\par
In response to comments by Commissioner Nowicki, Mr. Burton noted that staff responded to Commissioner Nowicki\rquote s email regarding the item associated with Keystone Road on his behalf and copied the Commissioners to the correspondence. He also indicated that the proposed amendment to the handbook stemmed from a disagreement regarding the handling of Commissioner Nowicki\rquote s proposed resolution concerning Flock cameras; and that Commissioner Nowicki wanted the resolution placed directly on the agenda for action, while he understood the Board's direction to be that the matter would first be discussed at a work session.\par
\par
Commissioner Peters expressed support for the existing process for the existing process for bringing items before the Board and indicated that she does not support the proposed amendment; whereupon, Chair Eggers noted the lack of support for the proposed change and encouraged Commissioner Nowicki to continue bringing matters before the Board through the existing process.\par
\par
Later in the meeting, Mr. Burton related that he misspoke and did not respond to Commissioner Nowicki\rquote s email regarding Keystone Road; and that he forwarded his response to staff for review; whereupon, he apologized for the oversight.\par
\par
\ul Automated License Plate Reader Resolution (Commissioner Nowicki)\ulnone\par
\par
Chair Eggers indicated that the second item under New Business is a proposed resolution regarding automated license plate readers (ALPRs); and that the Board previously discussed the matter at a work session attended by the Sheriff; whereupon, he referenced concerns raised by members of the public regarding access to and potential misuse of ALPR data and opened the floor for further discussion.\par
\par
In response to comments and queries by Commissioner Latvala, Sheriff Bob Gualtieri explained that, if the Board passed a resolution prohibiting ALPR cameras on County property or rights-of-way, the Sheriff's Office would relocate the affected cameras; that approximately 300 stationary ALPR cameras are located throughout Pinellas County, including approximately 60 on County rights-of-way; and that an executive order issued by the Governor required the Florida Department of Transportation to revoke permits for cameras on its rights-of-way but did not require the removal of cameras elsewhere. He also expressed confidence that the State Legislature would pass legislation addressing ALPR use, including data retention, access, and auditing requirements.\par
\par
Responding to an additional query by Commissioner Latvala, Attorney White indicated that the County could control the placement of cameras on its own infrastructure, although she would need to examine whether the County could regulate the Sheriff's Office's handling of ALPR data. She also noted that records retention schedules are established by the State; and that the County most likely could not override those requirements. Commissioner Latvala then then expressed a preference to await legislative action, suggested including the matter in the County's legislative priorities and those of the Florida Association of Counties (FAC), and indicated that the Board could revisit the issue in May, if necessary.\par
\par
In response to a query by Chair Eggers, Sheriff Gualtieri discussed improvements to the Sheriff's Office's auditing procedures, including the implementation of an automated auditing tool that allows for more comprehensive review of past ALPR queries. He also expressed support for incorporating best practices into State law to establish consistent requirements for agencies utilizing ALPR technology; whereupon, he noted that the legal question concerning the use of ALPRs involves their tracking capabilities, which would be a matter for the courts to determine.\par
\par
Commissioner Flowers expressed support\f1\fs22 \f0\fs24 for the continued use of ALPRs, citing their public safety benefits while acknowledging concerns regarding improper use of the technology. She also discussed potential improvements to protocols governing data access, review, and retention and related that ALPRs would be discussed through FAC's Health, Safety, & Justice Committee.\par
\par
Responding to comments by Commissioner Flowers, Sheriff Gualtieri clarified that the cameras utilized by the Sheriff\rquote s Office, with the exception of dash cameras, have no video capability; that the Office policy dictates that only still photographs are to be captured; that he possesses control over the access, regulation, and distribution of his office\rquote s data; and that various entities support the utilization of ALPR technology and wish to ensure the incorporation of related best practices. Sheriff Gualtieri also noted that ALPR cameras are motion activated; that the capture of collateral environmental images is incidental; and that the intent of the cameras is to photograph license plates.\par
\par
Chair Eggers then indicated that he does not sense further desire for discussion from the members; whereupon, Mr. Burton related that several members inquired about ALPRs during conversations regarding the County\rquote s State legislative program; and that staff intend to reach out to the Sheriff\rquote s Office to examine supportive options as part of the legislative program.\cf1\f2\fs22\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24 Ordinance No. 26-29 adopted, approving Case No. FLU-25-10. The Local Planning Agency recommended approval of the request, and staff concurred. Two emails in opposition have been received.\par
\par
Ms. Revie indicated that Agenda Item Nos. 38 and 39 are companion items; whereupon, referring to a PowerPoint presentation containing photographs and maps, Zoning and Project Management Division Director Michael Schoderbock pointed out the location of the subject property and explained that the request is for both a Future Land Use Map amendment and a zoning change.\par
\par
Mr. Schoderbock described the current and proposed land use and zoning designations; whereupon, he noted that the proposed use for the site is a restaurant and bar, which would be subject to a development agreement containing the following restrictions:\par
\par
\pard\fi-360\li360\f1\'b7\tab\f0 The property shall be limited to a restaurant, bar, and other accessory uses that directly support the principal permitted use.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 The property shall be developed substantially in conformance with the concept plan.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 No amplified music shall be permitted on the property.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 The observation deck shown on the concept plan shall be for patrons of the restaurant only and shall not be open to the public.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Development standards shall be limited by the concept plan, including building size, impervious coverage, setbacks, and buffering.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 No residential uses shall be permitted.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 Any dock facilities shall comply with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection\rquote s impaired waterbody criteria for Lake Tarpon.\par
\pard\par
Mr. Schoderbock also indicated that the following additional restrictions were recommended by the Local Planning Agency (LPA):\par
\par
\pard\fi-360\li360\f1\'b7\tab\f0 The existing boat ramp shall be removed from the property prior to issuance of the certificate of occupancy.\par
\f1\'b7\tab\f0 No dock facilities may be located on the north side of the property.\par
\pard\par
Mr. Schoderbock reviewed a concept plan associated with the case, including details regarding the proposed building\rquote s footprint, ingress and egress, buffering, impervious surface ratio (ISR), floor area ratio (FAR), building height, and maximum occupancy; whereupon, he described the surrounding land uses and noted that while the property is currently vacant, it was previously utilized as a mobile home park.\par
\par
Mr. Schoderbock discussed potential traffic impacts and flood risk, noting that the property is within the Coastal Storm Area, the Coastal High Hazard Area (CHHA), and the Pinellas County Coastal 100-Year Flood Zone, which requires a finished floor elevation of 11.3 feet for any development; whereupon, he related that the proposal is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and compatible with the area\rquote s mix-use character; that staff recommends approval; and that the LPA also unanimously recommended approval of both cases.\par
\par
Responding to queries by Chair Eggers, Mr. Schoderbock indicated that the last mobile home was removed from the property in approximately 2008; that no structures have been placed on the property since then; and that no other plans for development have been received; whereupon, he noted that a restriction regarding docks on the south side of the property could be added to the development agreement.\par
\par
In response to further queries, Mr. Schoderbock confirmed that no amplified music would be allowed anywhere on the property. He also noted that the applicant will be required to file deed restrictions as part of site plan review; and that the only way to remove such restrictions would be through Board approval.\par
\par
Following a request by Chair Eggers, Mr. Schoderbock noted that there is a conservation easement as well as a vacant County right-of-way between the subject property and adjacent properties to the north; and that the right-of-way would not be developed; whereupon, he related that the applicant is proposing a six-foot tall fence, hedging, and trees to provide buffering along the north and south sides of the property.\par
\par
Responding to queries by Chair Eggers regarding traffic impacts, Mr. Schoderbock provided information related to U.S. Highway 19 North, noting that it is under the jurisdiction of the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT); that permitting through FDOT would be required to place any access restrictions on the road; and that FDOT would be included in the site planning process.\par
\par
In response to a query by Commissioner Scott, Mr. Schoderbock indicated that concerns were expressed by citizens at the LPA hearing regarding noise and trash issues and possible bald eagle activity; whereupon, he related that while there is an eagle\rquote s nest on the property, federal records list it as abandoned; that County environmental staff visited the property on October 14; and that no evidence of bald eagle activity was found.\par
\pard\tx1340\par
\pard Upon the Chair\rquote s call for the applicant, Brian Aungst, Clearwater, appeared and noted that he is present on behalf of the applicant, Trent Road LLC. Mr. Aungst explained that the intent of the proposal is to activate the site in a manner more compatible with the area\rquote s mix-use character; whereupon, he emphasized that the current site usage is not allowed under the Comprehensive Plan; and that the purpose of the development agreement is to ensure compliance with regulations related to stormwater quality, drainage, retention, and flood mitigation. \par
\par
Mr. Aungst also discussed the existing conditions on the site, noting that if any eagle nesting activity were observed, it would be addressed during the permitting stage, along with ingress and egress concerns; whereupon, he provided details related to the proposed development standards and indicated that the applicant is not opposed to restricting docks on the south side of the property.\par
\par
Upon the Chair\rquote s call for public comment, the following individuals appeared and expressed their concerns:\par
\par
Andrew Moranville, Palm Harbor\par
Valerie Speer, Palm Harbor\par
\pard\tx3268 Ron Speer, Palm Harbor\par
\pard Robert Severance, Palm Harbor\par
\par
In rebuttal, Mr. Aungst addressed concerns raised regarding ingress and egress, noise, wildlife activity, and the neighboring hotel, noting that there is no access to the property from Trent Road; whereupon, he reiterated that there will be no amplified or live music on the property; and that, during the permitting process, any wildlife concerns would be addressed in conjunction with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS).\par
\par
In response to queries by Chair Eggers, Mr. Schoderbock pointed out the locations of Trent Road and Timberlane Road, noting that the section of Trent Road which runs north-south is part of the subject property; that a private ingress-egress easement would be required for that portion of the road; and that signage could be erected to indicate the remaining private portion of the road; whereupon, he provided brief information regarding easements, the existing eagle\rquote s nest, and USFWS involvement during the site planning process.\par
\par
Responding to queries and comments by Commissioner Flowers, Mr. Schoderbock indicated that any maintenance agreements related to Trent Road would be between the property owners; and that Timberlane Road is the only access to the subject property and neighboring residences from U.S. Highway 19 North; whereupon, he provided details regarding the site plan map, hours of operation for outdoor areas, and the location of the eagle\rquote s nest.\par
\par
Following additional comments by Mr. Speer, Mr. Aungst indicated that the applicant will maintain their portion of Trent Road to the extent that is required; whereupon, in response to a query by Commissioner Scherer, he briefly discussed potential deterrents to accidental ingress onto the private portion of Trent Road.\cf1\f2\fs22\par
}

Conduct a public hearing and adopt the proposed amendments to the County Drug Paraphernalia Ordinance revising County Code Section 86-106, clarifying definitions to align with recent statutory changes to exclude products for fentanyl analogue and xylazine testing to promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents.
· In 2005, Pinellas County adopted resolution 05-195 to establish a Drug Paraphernalia Abatement Task Force (Task Force) to review community impacts. As a result of Task Force recommendations, the County adopted Ordinance 06-73, to help mitigate possible community impact and limit access by youth.
· Since adopting the ordinance, Pinellas has experienced the impacts of the prescription drug epidemic and the resulting opioid crisis from the illicit drug market, with 266 overdose-related deaths in 2025.
· In recent years, fentanyl, fentanyl analogues, and xylazine have emerged as a major drugs of concern driving overdoses nationwide. Often individuals are unaware of the presence of these substances resulting in severe risk of poisoning, hospitalization, and death.
· In response to this growing threat, the State of Florida passed House Bill 477 revising drug paraphernalia definitions to add exclusions of products for xylazine testing effective July 1, 2026 in order to help reduce possible overdoses and save lives. Fentanyl and fentanyl analogue testing products were excluded by the State of Florida and Pinellas County in 2023.
· Based on the statutory change, Pinellas County is seeking to quickly incorporate the same exclusion locally to help protect the health and safety of our residents.
· Human Services anticipates a full review of this ordinance in the coming year to receive updated stakeholder input, assess updates and ongoing needs, and define recommended changes.
· This ordinance change has no fiscal impact to Pinellas County. Additionally, this change creates no new business impacts.

action_text:
Recommend adoption of a resolution to not exempt property under the Live Local Act Property Tax Exemption (The Act).
· Section 196.1978(3), Florida Statutes, commonly known as The Act, requires the Pinellas County Property Appraiser (PAO) to exempt rental properties with households whose annual household income is between 80.0%-120.0% of the Area Median Income (AMI) within a Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) from ad valorem taxes.
· With the commencement of the 2027 tax roll, taxing authorities may “opt-out” of providing The Act to certain rental units in multifamily projects that would otherwise qualify for the 80.0% to 120.0% Tax Exemption if the previous three (3) years of the Shimberg Center for Housing Studies Annual Report (Shimberg Annual Report) identifies a surplus of affordable and available units.
· On November 18, 2025, the Board of County Commissioners (Board) approved a Resolution to “opt-out” for 2026, but a new resolution is required to continue it through 2027.
· The County finds that the previous three (3) years of the Shimberg Annual Report identifies a surplus of affordable and available units within the Tampa St. Petersburg- Clearwater MSA, in which Pinellas County is located, for those households that meet the income criteria for the 80.0% to 120.0% Tax Exemption.
· Pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes, the County remains eligible for the “opt-out” election and, pending approval of this Resolution, elects not to exempt properties eligible for the exemption and requests that PAO not grant any such exemptions.
· This Resolution applies to all ad valorem property tax levies imposed by the County. If approved, it will take effect on January 1, 2027, and will expire or be renewed pursuant to the provisions Section 196.1978(3)(o), Florida Statutes.
· The adoption of this Resolution has no fiscal impact on the County...Body
